source_refs.file: B1专八历年真题+听力+解析/01.历年真题+解析/2015年专八真题+音频+解析/2015年英语专八真题解析.pdf

sentences.en: Now, both the government and the Opposition party agree that state schools are not good enough.
sentences.zh: 现在，政府与反对党都认为，公立学校还不够好。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: And the Opposition is coming up with some new proposals of their own to improve them.
sentences.zh: 反对党正在提出自己的一些新方案，试图改善这些学校。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: But is their approach really all that different from the government’s?
sentences.zh: 但是，他们的做法真的与政府的做法有那么大的不同吗？
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: Today, we have Theresa May, the Shadow Education Secretary from the Opposition, with us on the radio show.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们邀请到反对党的影子教育大臣特雷莎·梅，做客本台广播节目。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: Good afternoon, Theresa.
sentences.zh: 下午好，特雷莎。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: Good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 下午好。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: Can I remind you of what John Major said, only a few years ago, when he was prime Minister?
sentences.zh: 我想提醒您，几年前约翰·梅杰还是首相时说过的一番话。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: He said.
sentences.zh: 他说。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: “We should give people opportunity and choice.
sentences.zh: “我们应该给人们机会和选择。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: I don’t mean some people.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是某些人。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: I mean everyone, opportunity for all.” Well, that is precisely what the present government is saying: opportunity for all.
sentences.zh: 我指的是每个人，要让所有人都有机会。”而这正是现任政府所说的：人人都有机会。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: The hallmark of this government is that what they say and what they actually do is always different.
sentences.zh: 这个政府的特点就是，他们说的与实际做的总是不一样。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: And that’s no different in education.
sentences.zh: 在教育方面也是如此。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: What we see from the present government is they may talk about opportunity for all, they may talk about choice, but actually they are cutting opportunity and reducing choice.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，现任政府也许口口声声说人人都有机会、人人都有选择，但实际上，他们正在减少机会、缩小选择范围。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: And what I think is most damaging is that actually they are giving a message: don’t bother.
sentences.zh: 我认为，破坏性最大的是，他们实际上在传递一种信息：别费力了。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: If you're from a state school there are barriers to be put in your place.
sentences.zh: 如果你来自公立学校，就会有重重障碍挡在你面前。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: But, this is far from the truth: universities have been doing a very great deal to encourage state school pupils to apply.
sentences.zh: 但事实远非如此：大学一直在付出很大努力，鼓励公立学校的学生申请入学。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: The point is that we still haven’t got enough state school pupils applying to our leading universities.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，申请顶尖大学的公立学校学生仍然不够多。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: But your government had eighteen years to get more of them into Oxbridge.
sentences.zh: 可是，你们执政了十八年，本来可以让更多这样的学生进入牛津和剑桥。

w.m: n.牛津与剑桥两所大学的合称

sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: And indeed we increased the number of young people in this country going into university from one in eight to one in three.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们让本国年轻人的大学入学比例从八分之一提高到了三分之一。

w.m: phr.每八人中有一人；八分之一

sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: The number of state pupils being accepted by Oxford and Cambridge, and other leading universities, the proportion of state pupils has actually increased, but there is a problem in many of our secondary schools, of expectations, and it’s the present Government that has been levelling down expectations, rather than raising them.
sentences.zh: 被牛津、剑桥及其他顶尖大学录取的公立学校学生比例，实际上已经提高了。但是，我们许多中学的学生对未来的期望存在问题；当前政府一直在降低这些期望，而不是提高它们。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: But I was talking about pupils from state schools going to the so-called elite universities.
sentences.zh: 但我说的是，进入所谓精英大学的公立学校学生。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: That didn’t go up during your time.
sentences.zh: 你们执政期间，这个比例并没有上升。
sentences.speaker: I

sentences.en: The number from the state schools, who are going to leading universities, has increased over the years, but there is still an issue about ensuring that pupils from our state schools apply to go into the universities, and if you look at the Oxford figures, for example, you see that the percentage of students applying to Oxford from the state schools is about 1%, whereas from the private schools it’s over 4.5%, so that, you know, that’s the problem, it’s expectations in the state system that have been driven down by this Government over the years.
sentences.zh: 这些年来，来自公立学校、进入顶尖大学的学生人数有所增加，但如何确保公立学校学生积极申请大学，仍是一个问题。以牛津的数据为例，公立学校学生申请牛津的比例大约是百分之一，而私立学校学生的这一比例超过百分之四点五。所以，你看，问题就在这里：这些年来，公立教育体系中的期望一直被本届政府压低。
sentences.speaker: T

sentences.en: In Theresa’s view, what is the present government doing?
sentences.zh: 在特雷莎看来，现任政府正在做什么？
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: What is the problem in secondary schools now?
sentences.zh: 现在中学存在什么问题？
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: What can we learn from the interview?
sentences.zh: 我们能从访谈中了解到什么？
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: What contribution does Theresa think her party has made in education?
sentences.zh: 特雷莎认为，她所在的政党在教育方面作出了什么贡献？
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: What’s the man’s focus in this part of the interview?
sentences.zh: 在访谈的这一部分，男士关注的重点是什么？
sentences.speaker: announcer
